episodes.title: The Woman at the Center of America's Mother God Cult.
episodes.description:
Amy Carlson, known to her followers as “Mother God,” built a spiritual movement that promised enlightenment, healing, and a path to a higher dimension. But behind the colorful livestreams, unusual beliefs, and devoted followers was a disturbing story that ended in a police investigation and a shocking discovery in Colorado.

In this documentary, we investigate the rise of Love Has Won, Amy Carlson’s journey to becoming its central figure, the beliefs that shaped the group, and the events that brought national attention to the movement.
How did a woman come to be worshipped as God? What drew people into her world? And what happened inside the group before authorities intervened?

Watch until the end as we examine the case, the people involved, and the questions that remain.

episodes.title: The Cult Leader Who Built an Empire in Arkansas
episodes.description:
Tony Alamo built what looked like a powerful religious ministry—but behind the church was an enormous empire of businesses, properties, followers, and money.

From Hollywood to Arkansas, Alamo’s organization grew to include restaurants, clothing stores, gas stations, grocery stores, hog farms, construction companies, and even a famous rhinestone fashion business. His followers worked for little or no wages while Alamo fought the government in court over labor laws, taxes, and control of the organization.

Then everything began to collapse.

The IRS pursued millions in unpaid taxes. Federal marshals seized the Arkansas compound. Susan Alamo’s body mysteriously disappeared from her mausoleum. Tony Alamo became a fugitive before eventually being arrested and sent to federal prison. Years later, a new investigation into abuse inside his ministry would lead to a 175-year federal prison sentence.

But even prison did not completely end the empire.

Survivors later went to court and helped uncover who truly controlled the properties and wealth hidden behind the names of followers and church organizations. In 2013, a federal judge ruled that Tony Alamo was the true owner of properties held in other people's names, leading to further seizures.

This is the story of Tony Alamo—the preacher who turned a ministry into an empire, fought the federal government for decades, and left behind one of the darkest religious scandals in Arkansas history.

Watch until the end to discover how the courts finally answered the question: **Who really owned the Alamo empire?

episodes.title: The Arizona Cult Accused of Exploiting Its Own Members
episodes.description:
Deep in southern Arizona, the Global Community Communications Alliance built a secluded religious community around spiritual teachings, communal living, businesses, and healthcare organizations.

This documentary investigates the group's history, the rise of Gabriel of Urantia, its move to southern Arizona, and allegations involving unpaid labor, financial control, healthcare, family separation, and millions of dollars connected to affiliated organizations.

We examine the controversy surrounding Soulistic Hospice, former members' accounts, and multiple lawsuits that have brought renewed attention to the community.

These allegations have not necessarily been proven in court and are presented as allegations based on reporting and court filings.

episodes.title: The Alabama Cult Leader Who Ordered His Followers to Kill for God
episodes.description:
In 1912, an Alabama preacher named John Samuel Barker reportedly claimed that he was the Christ—and hundreds of people were drawn into the movement that became known as the Barkerites.

But the story took a darker turn when Barker's followers were accused of abandoning their families, following extreme religious teachings, and even believing that certain people were possessed by the devil.

Years later, Barker left Alabama for Oklahoma with members of his family. In 1924, a two-year-old boy named Artemus Barker disappeared from a camp in Watonga, Oklahoma. His father, Joseph C. Barker, was eventually convicted of first-degree manslaughter after his young daughter testified that she had witnessed her father kill the child.

But one question remains: Was Artemus's death connected to the strange teachings of John Samuel Barker?

The surviving court record proves what happened in the Oklahoma case—but it does not prove that Barker ordered anyone to kill a child. Much of that connection survives only through decades-old local memories and conflicting stories.

In this episode, we examine the disturbing story of John Samuel Barker, the Barkerites, the 1924 Oklahoma investigation, the testimony of a six-year-old girl, and the mystery surrounding a cult leader who claimed to be Christ.

How much of the Barkerite story can actually be proven—and what remains buried in legend?

Watch until the end and decide for yourself.

episodes.title: Religious Leaders Who Ran Cults And Scams In America: Tony Alamo
episodes.description:
Tony Alamo presented himself as a powerful prophet, built a multimillion-dollar ministry, and attracted followers by offering food, shelter, and a sense of belonging to people who felt forgotten by society. But behind the public image was a deeply controlling organization that would eventually face allegations of financial exploitation, forced labor, and the abuse of young girls.

In this episode, we trace Tony Alamo’s journey from Bernie Lazar Hoffman, a man with a criminal past and failed music ambitions, to the self-proclaimed prophet known as “Papa Tony.” We explore his rise alongside his wife Susan Alamo, the growth of their ministry, the controversial business empire that followed, and the legal battles that eventually exposed serious problems within the organization.

After Susan’s death, Alamo’s control over his followers became even more extreme. His teachings were used to justify secret marriages involving underage girls, while fear, isolation, and religious authority made it incredibly difficult for members to seek outside help.

The story reaches its climax with the 2008 federal raid, the arrest of Tony Alamo, and the testimony of five women who described what they experienced while inside the ministry. In 2009, Alamo was convicted on all ten federal counts and sentenced to 175 years in prison.

This is more than the story of one cult leader. It is a disturbing look at how religious authority, isolation, financial exploitation, and fear can allow abuse to remain hidden for decades—and how survivors ultimately helped bring the system down.

Watch until the end to discover how Tony Alamo’s empire was built, how it survived years of legal scrutiny, and what finally brought his decades-long reign to an end.

episodes.title: Religious Leaders Who Ran Cults And Scams In America: Warren Jeffs
episodes.description:
RELIGIOUS LEADERS WHO RAN CULTS AND SCAMS IN AMERICA: WARREN JEFFS
Warren Jeffs inherited far more than a religious title. As leader of the Fundamentalist Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-Day Saints (FLDS), he inherited a tightly controlled religious community in which his authority extended into marriage, education, family life, and local government.
For years, Jeffs was treated by followers as a prophet whose instructions were believed to come directly from God. Behind that authority was a system that prosecutors and survivors said enabled the abuse and exploitation of children and vulnerable members of the community.
This documentary follows Jeffs's rise from FLDS school principal to the organization's most powerful leader, the structure of the communities of Hildale, Utah, and Colorado City, Arizona, the creation of the Yearning for Zion Ranch in Texas, and the investigations that eventually brought his actions into a courtroom.
We examine:
• Warren Jeffs's childhood and upbringing inside the FLDS
• His father's transformation of the church into a system centered around one prophet
• Jeffs's rise to power after Rulon Jeffs's death
• The FLDS system of arranged and plural marriages
• The role of religious authority in controlling members' lives
• The allegations made by survivors, including his nephew Brent Jeffs
• Jeffs's appearance on the FBI's Ten Most Wanted list and his eventual capture
• The 2008 raid on the Yearning for Zion Ranch
• The evidence presented against Jeffs at his 2011 Texas trial
• His conviction and life sentence
• The legal battles surrounding the FLDS community and its property
• The continuing influence Jeffs has had over some followers from prison
This is not an attack on an entire religion or every person who has belonged to the FLDS. It is an examination of one religious leader, the documented criminal cases against him, and the institutional structure that allowed his authority to become extraordinarily powerful.
The Warren Jeffs case raises a disturbing question: What happens when one person's religious authority becomes so absolute that questioning him is treated as questioning God?
Watch until the end for the broader lesson behind Jeffs's story—and why removing a leader doesn't necessarily destroy the system that gave him power.
DISCLAIMER: This video is intended for documentary, educational, and historical discussion. Allegations are identified as such, while criminal convictions and court-determined facts are presented as established legal outcomes. Viewer discretion is advised due to discussion of abuse and crimes involving minors.

episodes.title: Religious Leaders Who Ran Cults And Scams In America: Jim Baker
episodes.description:
Jim Bakker rose from a young preacher to one of America’s most powerful televangelists, building a massive religious broadcasting empire and Heritage USA, a Christian theme park that attracted millions of visitors.
But behind the television cameras was a financial system that prosecutors said depended on promises that could never be fulfilled. Thousands of viewers purchased lifetime partnerships, believing they were securing annual hotel stays. Instead, the scheme helped fuel a financial collapse that eventually led to a federal fraud conviction and prison sentence.
In this documentary, we examine Jim Bakker’s rise, the PTL Club, Heritage USA, the lifetime partnership scheme, the scandal that brought his empire down, his conviction, and his controversial return to television decades later.
We also look at the broader question: How can religious authority create an environment where financial misconduct can continue for years before anyone intervenes?
This video is part of our series examining controversial religious leaders, alleged cult-like organizations, financial scandals, and the abuse of trust in America.

episodes.title: The American Doomsday Cult That Believed Its Leader Was God
episodes.description:
For more than five decades, the movement once known as the Children of God has repeatedly changed its name, structure, and leadership—yet continued to exist.
Founded in 1968 by David Brandt Berg, the group grew from a small counterculture religious movement into an international organization. Its history would later become associated with controversial teachings, abusive practices, the sexual exploitation of members, and allegations involving children.
This documentary examines the evolution of the Children of God → Family of Love → The Family → Family International, and the disturbing policies that shaped its history.
We also examine the landmark 1995 UK High Court case in which Justice Alan Ward made serious findings concerning the organization's treatment of children, the rise of Karen Zerby after Berg's death, and the tragic story of her son Ricky Rodriguez, who became a central figure in the movement's history.
Despite scandals, judicial scrutiny, leadership changes, and a dramatic decline in membership, the organization did not disappear. Instead, it reorganized, decentralized, and continued under a new structure.
How does an organization survive for nearly six decades despite everything that happened inside it?
This is the story of The Family International.
Disclaimer: This documentary examines documented organizational history, court findings, and allegations involving former members and leadership. It does not suggest that every person who belonged to the movement participated in or was aware of the abuses discussed.
